concept.learning_outcome: Identify the actual water problem before choosing treatment; understand treatment jobs and limits; compare historical/global systems by function and evidence; build a practical multi-use system plan; transfer diagnosis and evidence-literacy principles elsewhere.
concept.central_question: What is the water problem, what can each method actually do, and what evidence shows the claim is the right size?
major_principles: Clear water is not automatically safe water.
Water treatment is a chain, not a magic ingredient.
Source protection is part of treatment.
Traditional and modern describe context, not truth value.
Match the claim to the mechanism and evidence.
A successful build is not proof; test the result.
concept.transfer_the_principle_summary: Diagnose before prescribing; match solutions to actual problems; match claims to mechanism/evidence; use function before form when comparing treatment options and substitutions.
